summary:
Road to Mars is a co-op space survival and flight simulator for up to 6 players, made by team El Tarabeza El Aaleya. The crew shares a room code and works together to get a ship from a NASA launch pad to Mars. There is no impostor.

Prepare: Pick a rocket, a science payload, and the amounts of food, oxygen and fuel. Heavier loads mean a slower trip and faster fuel burn.

Survive: On the 2D ship, tasks like farming, water recycling, fuel production and repairs keep resources from running out.
Fly: Any player can pilot in 3D, dodging and shooting real NASA asteroids for fuel and science points.
Decide: The crew can land on the Moon for extra food, or dump cargo or vote to eject a player (who stays on as a 0 kg ghost) when the ship is too heavy.
Finish: At 100% progress the crew wins and gets an engineering report, then Free-Play unlocks. The game never ends suddenly.
details:
What it does
Road to Mars is a co-op space survival and flight simulator for up to 6 players. The crew shares a room code and works together to take a spacecraft from a NASA launch pad to Mars. It borrows the feel of Among Us, with a 2D ship, tasks and emergency meetings, but there is no impostor. The whole crew works against the ship’s failing systems instead of each other.

Before launch, the crew chooses a rocket (Electron, Falcon 9 or SLS Block 1B), a science payload, and the amounts of food, oxygen and fuel. A live readout shows total mass, Δv, thrust-to-weight and travel time, so every kilogram has a visible cost. During the mission, players do tasks inside a 10-room ship: farming, water recycling, turning CO₂ into fuel, and repairs. Any player can switch to a 3D cockpit and fly through real NASA asteroids such as Bennu and Itokawa, shooting them for fuel and science points. The crew can also land on the Moon for extra food, or dump cargo or vote to eject a player when the ship is too heavy. At 100% progress the crew wins and receives an engineering report, then Free-Play unlocks.

Benefits and impact
The game teaches mission planning in a hands-on way. Players learn that mass, fuel, food and oxygen are linked, that life support is a closed loop, and that deep-space trips depend on teamwork and trade-offs. It is meant to make space engineering approachable and social for students and general audiences.

Tools
Built with Nodejs and Typescript using NASA asteroid data as the basis for the in-game asteroids.

Creativity
We combined three things: a social task-based ship, a 6-axis flight simulator, and an engineering weight-and-fuel model. We also added local humor (Romy cheese as in-game food) and a forgiving design with emergency guide arrows and a Free-Play mode, so the game never ends suddenly.

Factors we considered
Teaching real engineering trade-offs while keeping the game fun, cooperation instead of competition, fair pacing for first-time players, and keeping the 2D and 3D parts connected so tasks and flying affect each other.
